bilateralTree.title: Cladogram of the bilateral lattice
bilateralTree.ariaLabel: Cladogram of the Pandoran bilateral lattice, with the Na'vi as the aberrant branch
bilateralTree.ancestorSub: 6 limbs · 4 eyes · paired queues · carbon-fibre bone · opercula

characterMatrix.title: Character matrix → the most parsimonious tree
characterMatrix.ariaLabel: Pandoran cladogram built from the character matrix
characterMatrix.stepsParsimony: Fewest steps — carbon-fibre bone and the queue evolve just once
characterMatrix.stepsPhenetic: Steps explode — carbon-fibre bone and the queue must evolve twice, on two worlds
characterMatrix.synapNote: Bold branch: where carbon-fibre bone + the queue appear once, binding the whole branch into one lineage.
characterMatrix.hint: Tap to move the Na'vi. Parsimony picks the tree needing the fewest changes — and that tree nests the Na'vi deep inside the Pandoran six-limbed branch, not beside humans.

longBranch.title: Long-branch attraction
longBranch.trueNote: Ikran and toruk sit on two separate lineages. Long branch = fast evolution, heaping up independent flight traits.
longBranch.inferredNote: The two long branches are pulled together at the base — parsimony mistakes chance resemblance for kinship.
longBranch.hint: On Earth, molecular data corrects this error. Pandora has no molecules — so a morphology-only tree stays vulnerable to exactly this trap.

limbField.title: One toolkit, three switches
limbField.hint: The same Hox toolkit. Switching off one limb field's enhancer deletes that pair outright — it does not fuse them. This is exactly how snakes lost their legs on Earth.

hoxMap.title: The Hox address system
hoxMap.prompt: Hover or tap a gene to see the body region it labels.
hoxMap.hint: The order of the genes on the shelf matches the order of the body regions they label. A Hox gene does not build a part — it stamps an address. Move a label and you move a body part, without redesigning the part itself.

hox1.note: Specifies head structure and double sensory organs.

hox2.note: Addresses the breathing vents and primary neck segments.

hox3.note: Switches on the first pair of appendages, forming wings.

hox4.note: Forms the central ribcage and carbon-composite support skeleton.

hox5.note: Controls development of the rear crawling/clinging claws.

hox6.note: Specifies the tail tip and neural queue connection interface.

replayTape.title: Replay the tape
replayTape.hint: The role converges every time — because physics writes the job description. But the substrate that fills it is history's call, and history never repeats.

convergence.title: Same job, different substrate
convergence.jobHint: In Job mode both wear the same pounce — the spring-loaded haunch, the grasping forelimb, the forward hunting eyes. Ambush predation has a shape, and any lineage that takes up the trade is pulled toward it.
convergence.tellsHint: In Tells mode, look again at the thanator: six limbs where the cat has four, four eyes where it has two, breathing slits down the flank. The role is Earth's; the animal is emphatically not.

nichePartition.title: One forest, divided into floors
nichePartition.prompt: Click a layer to see who feeds there.
nichePartition.hint: Competitive exclusion says two species cannot share one niche. The answer is not to share a niche — it is to split it into floors, each species at its own height, feeding its own way.

high.how: Reaches the high leaves no one else can crop.

mid.how: Strips foliage at mid-height, moving in herds.

low.how: Crops tender understorey shoots near the floor.

canopy.name: Canopy (High)
canopy.role: High-altitude apex predator, nesting in the emergent peaks and hunting canopy flyers.

midstory.name: Mid-story (Middle)
midstory.role: Agile, small-winged flocking foragers, feeding on mid-altitude insects and seeds.

floor.name: Forest Floor (Low)
floor.role: Ground pack hunters tracking hexapedes and forest-floor herbivores.
